Lessons.Title: From Visual Patterns to Numerical Patterns
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will analyze, describe, and extend numerical patterns that follow a rule.
Previously, you explored growing and repeating patterns and reasoned about the patterns using words, numbers, and operations. In this lesson, you investigate patterns in a geometric context and explore how the side lengths, area, perimeter, and other features of a rectangle change when the rectangle changes by a rule. In doing so, you practice looking for and making use of structure (MP7).
Core relationship: From visual to numerical growing patterns. Represent a shape's systematic growth with an input-step-to-quantity rule.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Number Talk: Patterns in Multiplication	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Growing Rectangles	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  More Growing Rectangles	 [OPTIONAL] (20 minutes); Activity 3:   No Grid This Time!	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Another Set of Rectangles	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: A rectangle pattern has 3, 5, 7 tiles. What is the next number?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): If the sequence continues 3, 5, 7, 9, what is the fifth count?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
